title: aid-auto-recovery-policy/1
description: The shape of the AUTO-mode recovery policy — defaults/policies/auto-recovery.yaml, and any project override of it at .aid-o/config/policies/auto-recovery.yaml. It is the single machine-readable authority for how an AUTO run classifies a stop and what reversible actions it may take before a person is involved. Two properties are load-bearing and are expressed here rather than left to prose: (1) `allowed_actions` is enum-constrained to the six defined action names, so an unknown action is a schema ERROR refused at load and never a silent no-op; (2) every stop class must carry both honesty axes — `detector` (does code detect this today?) and `ladder_entry` (who writes the ladder record?) — plus `ladder_entry_status`, which states whether that writer exists yet. A class may not be declared without an emitter unless it is UNCLASSIFIED, which by construction has none. The companion enforcement is scripts/tests/bats/test-auto-recovery-policy.bats, which validates the shipped policy against this schema, greps every named emitter to a real code site, and re-reads every `existing_loops` budget from the file it cites.

allOf.description: A policy may not declare the ladder wired while declaring the loader unimplemented. The pairing was previously accepted, which let one edited line claim a runtime that does not exist. This binds overrides too, which the test suite does not see.
The mirror: while the ladder is not wired, no class may claim its ladder entry is live. Nothing writes a ladder record, so `live` would be a false statement about code.

version.description: Policy schema generation. Bumped only on a breaking shape change.

ladder_runtime.description: Wiring truth, kept in the file the wiring is about: whether anything actually reads this policy yet, and where the code that will lands.

status.description: `not_wired` = the policy is shipped but no loader reads it and no code writes a ladder record. `wired` = both exist.

loader_contract.description: The decided behaviour of the loader for every degenerate input, written down before the loader exists so it is implemented against a decision rather than improvised. `implemented: false` states plainly that none of it runs yet.

loader_path.description: Repository-relative path of the file that will define the loader. The test derives whether the ladder is wired from this file rather than from `implemented`, so it must name plugin code and may not name a test.

loader_anchor.description: Name of the shell function the loader defines. The wired/not-wired answer is derived from a function definition with this name existing in `loader_path` in a file that also references this policy — a fact this policy cannot assert into being.

action_vocabulary.description: The CLOSED set of reversible actions, each with the sentence that says what it does. Exactly the six names — no more, no fewer — because `allowed_actions` is enum-constrained to them and a vocabulary entry with no enum slot would be unreachable.

stop_classes.description: The seven classes. UNCLASSIFIED is required because it is the default routing for anything unnamed — a policy without it could leave a stop with no route at all.

terminus_stages.description: What each terminus stage means. The order in a class's `terminus` array is the order they are tried; these are the definitions.

existing_loops.description: The ownership table: every retry loop that ALREADY exists in AID, declared with its own authority and its own budget location. `authority: existing` and `governed_by_ladder: false` are constants here — the whole point of the table is that the ladder declares these rather than rewiring them (P076 PM decision 4). `budget_value` + `budget_file` are what the drift test re-reads and compares.

supersedes.description: The earlier design documents this policy replaces, and exactly which of their sections it replaces. This lives in the SHIPPED policy on purpose: some of those documents are untracked (this repository gitignores `docs/`), so a claim recorded only in the document would be unreviewable and untestable wherever the document is absent. `tracked: false` obliges a `tracked_reason` — an untracked source may be superseded, but never silently.

emitter_site.description: One real code site that detects the condition. `anchor` is a literal substring that must be greppable in `file` — line numbers drift, the anchor is what the anti-decoration test actually asserts.

detector.description: Does CODE detect this condition at this commit, leaving a machine-readable trace? `mechanical` = yes, and `emitter` proves it. `instruction` = no; an agent following written instruction decides it.

ladder_entry.description: Who writes the ladder record — `mechanical` (from the emitting code site) or `instruction` (the AUTO-loop instruction routes the report into the ladder).

ladder_entry_status.description: Truth about that writer AT THIS COMMIT. `planned` = it does not exist yet. Marking a class `live` while nothing writes its entry is the decoration failure this field exists to prevent.

terminus.description: The terminus chain, in the order it is tried. Every class ends the same way: adjudicate, then ESCALATION, then an audited PM force. Neither shortening it NOR REORDERING it is a configuration option — the order is load-bearing, because `pm_force` is always a human act and a policy that reached it first would invert the whole ladder. The shipped policy's order is pinned by the test suite; this `const` is what pins it for a project override, which the test suite never sees.

emitting_class.description: A class with at least one real emitter site.

unclassified_class.description: UNCLASSIFIED — the default route. It has no emitter (it is defined as what is left over) and no allowed action at all: it goes straight to adjudication.

allowed_actions.description: Reversible actions this class may take before adjudication. ENUM-CONSTRAINED to the six names in `action_vocabulary`: anything else is a schema error refused at load, never a silent no-op. An empty array is legal and means 'no recovery — adjudicate immediately'.

budget.description: How much the class may spend before the terminus. Zero is legal configuration, not an error: a class entered with no budget goes straight to adjudication.

authority.description: Always `existing`. The ladder declares these loops; it does not own them.

governed_by_ladder.description: Always false. If a loop ever does become ladder-governed it stops being an entry in this table.

budget_kind.description: Where the number physically lives, which is what tells the drift test how to re-read it.

document.description: Repository-relative path of the superseded document.

tracked.description: Is the document under version control? `false` means the supersede marker inside it cannot be diff-reviewed, cannot roll back with this commit and is absent from a clone — which is why the section list is duplicated here, where it does ship.

marker_pattern.description: The literal string the supersede markers in the document carry, so the doc-side check has something to look for rather than a hand-written pattern in the test.

sections.description: The exact `## ` headings this policy replaces — and, by exclusion, the assertion that every OTHER section of that document is untouched.

allOf.description: An untracked supersede must say why it is untracked. Silence about a claim that does not ship is the failure mode this record exists to prevent.
